status: binds only with its agent adoption row in decisions/AGENT-ADOPTIONS.md (VIS-4 as amended by GOVERNANCE-SIMPLIFICATION-D10); read that ledger, never this field

predecessor.relation: this file is a new version beside the predecessor, which is not edited. The predecessor stays the binding of every run whose record binds it, and the base the URL origin/species policy v1 names by its reviewedSha256; which file a run binds is stated by REQ-polaris-generation-046 from specification version 2.6, never by this field

ownerDecision.recordedOn: bead syzygy-3efd.24 (description, 'Owner decision'); the decision packet it names is not in the repository
ownerDecision.authorizationBoundary: no secret detector, active-content rule or fail-closed rule is weakened; no dossier run is started; no repository is read by this decision; nothing is exposed beyond the tailnet; the choice does not itself change the policy file, which changes only by a reviewed successor recorded as an agent adoption with its revert command.
ownerDecision.ownerClass: RFC5-14's last owner-reserved change: content the secret-detection policy cannot classify today (configuration formats, nested documentation and the documents withheld by name) is admitted to the declared provider; the owner decided it. Everything else in this file is the agent's, adopted by an AGENT-ADOPTIONS.md row

reverses.what: the signed screening-scope-v2 choice of variant none (that act's line 'Chosen variant: none'), under which every docs-tree and licenses-tree path whose directory or file name has a word in docExcludedTokens is withheld, for the words in governanceTextTokens only: such a document is now classified governance-text by the governance-text-by-name rule and may be sent as that class. The words in withheldTokens keep variant none's treatment: still indeterminate
reverses.authority: ownerDecision above; the act record stays history and is not edited

notAdoptedFromTheOption.why: a text cell is a JSON string inside the notebook blob, so admitting it needs an extractor and a quotation rule that locates a cited span in the decoded cell rather than in the blob's bytes (REQ-polaris-generation-034 verifies every quotation against the pinned blob); the whole notebook body, outputs included, is not what the option admits. A .ipynb path stays indeterminate until a later successor states that extractor

notAdoptedFromTheOption.what: documents whose path carries a word in withheldTokens
notAdoptedFromTheOption.why: the option names design, architecture, ADR, RFC, spec and manifesto documents; governance, policy, security, conduct, doctrine and principle records are not named, so they stay indeterminate, and admitting them is asked of the owner. Decision records other than ADRs (the words decision and decisions) are held back with them until the owner says whether option A covers them; an ADR is admitted by the words adr and adrs

notAdoptedFromTheOption.what: run-on and camel-case names carrying a withheld, report or governance word
notAdoptedFromTheOption.why: a file such as SecurityPolicy.md, CodeOfConduct.md or DesignDoc.md folds to one word that is in no token list, so word matching alone would place it in project-documentation; the second stage therefore also refuses a documentation path any of whose segments contains a stem of withheldStems as a substring or has a word of evidenceWords, and project-documentation-extended refuses a segment containing a stem of governanceStems, so such paths stay indeterminate

publicSourceScope.purpose: classify and screen declared local dossier sources under SEC-5; target text is data, never policy
publicSourceScope.observedRepositories: the repository identity and full pinned commit declared in a dossier run; public and private sources are admitted without observation, registry, policy or provider-statement acts; owner placements apply only to the exact declared repository and commit they name

sourceVisibility.rule: visibility is declared for the exact repository and pinned commit in the dossier run, with its source attributed and labelled Inferred. Only an explicit public declaration gets public treatment. Private, missing or ambiguous declarations get private treatment; malformed declarations refuse. Syzygy makes no network request and uses no credential to verify visibility, and never infers it from a host, scheme, user name or credential use. No consent or act record supplies or overrides this declaration
sourceVisibility.privateSourceRules: a private repository is admitted as a declared local source under the same rules as a public one, except at three stricter sites: accessBoundary.networkEgressRoutes (no repository fetch and no host credential); secretRedaction.appliesTo (no redacted-span body: any detector match excludes the whole body in every class); and contentClassification code-structure and indeterminate rules (an excluded or withheld blob object id and size are never rendered or sent and remain only in permitted local check records and review packets). No detector, exclusion or private metadata rule is relaxed. A declared provider is required for content delivery under SEC-2; no separate egress consent is required
sourceVisibility.unchanged: every detector, scopeDetectors and configurationDetectors, matchAction, unclassifiableExclusion, sourceAdmission and its denied paths, contentClassification and its owner placements (except the code-structure rule and indeterminate's last sentence, above), instructionTextRule, targetMetadataRule, runProfileRule, activeContent and both of its exemptions, ingestBoundaries and ingestBoundaryRule, rawBodyHandling's storage (run-directory-only), logging (never), rendering (a generated editorial draft, never published) and machineResponse (never), inheritedRules, selfReferenceRule and prerequisite apply to a private repository exactly as to a public one. This scope states no retention period for a run directory under either visibility, and this version adds none. This policy declares screening rules, never observed provider transmission
sourceVisibility.agentSessions: SEC-2 and SEC-5 bind agents as well as Syzygy: only the declared provider may receive content, and secrets never leave. Briefs require agents to preserve screening and exclusion rules in their own reads and sends. Syzygy screens the content it reads, stores, renders and delivers; it cannot observe or attest an agent tool own transmissions or compliance, which are never presented as Observed
sourceVisibility.consequence: A private or undeclared-visibility local source is admitted with stricter whole-body exclusion and private withheld metadata protection; it may therefore yield more Unknown items. No provider transmission is observed merely because a provider is declared. The reason for the redaction rule: a retained redacted-span body shows every line but the withheld ones, and the whole body's content digest and Git object id stay recorded (RFC5-17), so a guess at a short withheld line can be confirmed against them offline; for a public repository the body is published already and this adds nothing, for a private one it would. Whole exclusion does not close the guess either: the content digest, and the Git object id, which is itself a digest of the whole body, are a confirmation oracle wherever a guesser knows the rest of the body (a private fork of a public upstream whose file differs by one secret line, a template, earlier public history), and the size narrows the secret's length. For a public repository the object id and size are code-structure, rendered on the dossier's pages and eligible as classified content for the declared provider. For a private repository this version withholds them for every blob excluded or withheld on any ground, a denied path, an indeterminate blob and a detector match among them: they are kept, if at all, only in the run directory's check records and its local review packets, and are never rendered or sent. What is left: the run directory itself and the operator's clone, which holds every object id, so whoever can read either can still confirm a guess; the pinned commit id, rendered on every discovery row and recorded in the run record, which is a digest of the commit header and the root tree and so of every object id in it, the withheld blob's included, a narrower confirmation oracle open only to a guesser who also knows the commit header (its author, dates, message and parent) and the rest of the tree, and one this scope cannot withhold; and a secret no detector matches in a body this scope admits, which is admitted and rendered under either visibility (SEC-5's general residual, unchanged here).
sourceVisibility.consentRecordMetadata: No launch consent record, dedicated recording reference or governance write is made for source admission. Repository identity, normalized locator, visibility and pinned revision are stored as Inferred run declarations in the local state directory, within the agent sessions write reach; they are not authorization records

publicSourceScope.ingestBoundaryRule: run-directory is a per-run directory under project:syzygy's state directory, outside git; human-html is a generated editorial draft shown only on the local daemon's draft view or as a static file in the run directory, never published; there is no cache, log, machine-json or walkthrough-record boundary for this scope

sourceAdmission.admittedSnapshot: the full commit pinned in the dossier run and the tree and blob objects reachable from its root tree; tag and branch names are locator provenance only
notAdmitted: any object outside the listed commits' root trees
sourceAdmission.resourceLimits: the existing bounded dossier object reader and declared finite run limits; removing a registry act changes no configured bound or breach result
sourceAdmission.deniedPaths: the base policy's sourceAdmission.deniedPathBasenames, deniedPathPrefixes, deniedPathSuffixes, deniedDirectoryNames and pathRuleScope apply, as this version extends them: every predecessor entry is kept and entries are only added

contentClassification.vocabulary: RFC5-14's closed vocabulary; this scope classifies into the classes in classesClassified only

rules.rule: the body of an admitted blob whose repository-relative path has exactly one segment and, compared after the fold the project-documentation rule uses (ASCII A-Z to a-z, nothing else folded, normalized or decoded), equals one of governanceTextPaths, after every screening step. The path is carried as admitted. No extractor runs: the class is by path and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans. Such a body is a target's own policy or doctrine text, which RFC5-14 places in governance-text; it is data and never governing policy for project:syzygy (RFC5-16, RFC3-30, selfReferenceRule). It is not in secretRedaction.redactedClasses, so any detector match excludes it whole, and no active-content exemption names it, so it is scanned as before. A consent record that does not list governance-text does not permit its egress; this policy confers no consent. A path that this rule and another class's rule both match has two classes and is indeterminate

normalized repository-relative paths, object ids and sizes of admitted snapshot entries, taken from Git tree metadata, with no body; except that, for a repository whose visibility is private (sourceVisibility), the object id and size of a blob that is excluded or withheld on any ground (a denied path, an indeterminate or unclassifiable blob, a detector match on its path or its body, active content, a strict-UTF-8, NUL or resource-limit failure, or any other exclusion) are not code-structure: they are kept, if at all, only in the run directory's check records and its local review packets, and are never rendered or carried in any egress

the body of an admitted blob whose final path segment ends with one of sourceExtensions, compared case-sensitively as ASCII, after every screening step. Configuration written in a listed extension (for example a .config.js file, setup.py or a .sh file) is therefore code-content. No extractor runs: the class is by extension and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans

the body of an admitted blob whose repository-relative path is matched by exactly one of the four path rules below, after every screening step. Matching compares a copy of the path with its ASCII letters A-Z folded to a-z and nothing else folded, normalized or decoded; the path is carried as admitted. A path with an empty, '.' or '..' segment, a backslash or a leading or trailing '/' matches nothing. No extractor runs: the class is by path and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans. The class is decided by these paths alone: a file's own claim about itself, or a directory name outside the four rules, places nothing in it (RFC5-14); an ownerPlacements entry is the owner's declared placement of named paths, which RFC5-14 lets the declared policy make

pathRules.rule: a path with one segment whose name, after removing rootStemNumericPrefix when it is present and then one suffix from documentSuffixes (any that fits), is one of rootStems

a path of two or more segments whose first segment is one of docTreeRoots, whose name ends with one of docTreeExtensions and is longer than it, in which no directory name after the first, and no file name without its extension, has a word in docExcludedTokens (a name is split into words at each character of docTokenSeparators, after the ASCII fold), and which is not a name ending in .txt that equals one of docTxtExcludedNames or starts with one of docTxtExcludedPrefixes

a path of exactly two segments whose first segment is one of licenseTreeRoots and whose name ends with one of licenseTreeSuffixes and is longer than it, and in which no word of the file name without its extension is in docExcludedTokens (split as for docs-tree)

a path that, after the same fold, equals one of the paths of an ownerPlacements entry (each listed already folded, so it is compared as given) whose repository is the repository the blob is read from and whose commits list the admitted commit it is read at. An entry places those paths and nothing else: it admits no repository, commit or object (the observation consent decides those), it is not inherited by any other repository or commit, and every screening step still applies to the body

rootStemNumericPrefix.note: exactly the ASCII characters listed in digits; no other character, including any Unicode digit, is a digit here

rules.disjointFromSourceExtensions: none of documentSuffixes, docTreeExtensions or licenseTreeSuffixes is in sourceExtensions, so no blob has two classes by extension; a blob matched here is never code-content
rules.notMapped: by these four path rules: nested and vendored documentation (a README below the root outside docs-tree and licenses-tree, unless an ownerPlacements entry names its path); root files named design, governance, security or code of conduct; docs-tree and licenses-tree paths whose directory or file name has a word in docExcludedTokens; build and tooling .txt files named in docTxtExcludedNames or docTxtExcludedPrefixes; committed reports and logs; and any other prose that no ownerPlacements entry names. Of these, classDecision's second stage places non-vendored nested documentation by the project-documentation-extended rule and the documents with a word in governanceTextTokens by the governance-text-by-name rule; vendored documentation, documents with a word in withheldTokens or evidenceWords or a stem of withheldStems (reports and logs among them), nested documents with a stem of governanceStems in a run-on word, and the excluded .txt files stay unplaced

rules.rule: computed from the classes of what a composite embeds (RFC5-14); a composite embedding any unclassified or excluded content is refused

the body of an admitted blob, after every screening step, whose final path segment ends with one of governanceTextExtensions and is longer than it, such that a word of some directory segment, or of the final segment with that extension removed, is in governanceTextTokens, and no word of any directory segment or of the final segment with that extension removed is in withheldTokens. A path with an empty, '.' or '..' segment, a backslash or a leading or trailing '/' matches nothing. Matching compares a copy of the path with its ASCII letters A-Z folded to a-z and nothing else folded, normalized or decoded, and words are split as the docs-tree rule splits them (at each character in docTokenSeparators); the path is carried as admitted. No extractor runs: the class is by path and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans. The rule is read only in classDecision's second stage. Besides word matching, the rule refuses a path any directory segment of which, or whose final segment with the matched extension or suffix removed, contains one of withheldStems as a substring of its folded copy, or has a word in evidenceWords: a run-on or camel-case name (SecurityPolicy.md, CodeOfConduct.md, audit-report.md) stays indeterminate. Such a body is a target's design, architecture, architecture-decision-record, request-for-comments, specification or manifesto text, which RFC5-14 places in governance-text and never in project-documentation; it is data and never governing policy for project:syzygy (RFC5-16, RFC3-30, selfReferenceRule). It is not redacted (secretRedaction.appliesTo), so any detector match, configurationDetectors included, excludes it whole, and no active-content exemption names it, so it is scanned as before

the body of an admitted blob, after every screening step, whose path is matched by at least one of the three path rules below and in which no word of any directory segment, and no word of the final segment with its matched extension or suffix removed, is in the four-rule project-documentation rule's docExcludedTokens, and no such segment contains one of governanceStems as a substring of its folded copy (DesignDoc.md and ArchitectureOverview.md stay indeterminate rather than misclassified). A path with an empty, '.' or '..' segment, a backslash or a leading or trailing '/' matches nothing. Matching compares a copy of the path with its ASCII letters A-Z folded to a-z and nothing else folded, normalized or decoded, and words are split as the docs-tree rule splits them (at each character in docTokenSeparators); the path is carried as admitted. No extractor runs: the class is by path and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans. The rule is read only in classDecision's second stage. Besides word matching, the rule refuses a path any directory segment of which, or whose final segment with the matched extension or suffix removed, contains one of withheldStems as a substring of its folded copy, or has a word in evidenceWords: a run-on or camel-case name (SecurityPolicy.md, CodeOfConduct.md, audit-report.md) stays indeterminate. The class is decided by these paths alone: a file's own claim about itself places nothing (RFC5-14). It is not redacted (secretRedaction.appliesTo), so any detector match, configurationDetectors included, excludes it whole, and activeContent.projectDocumentationExemption does not name it, so it is scanned as before

pathRules.rule: a path of any number of segments whose final segment ends with one of proseExtensions and is longer than it

a path of two or more segments whose final segment, read as the root-document rule reads a one-segment path (its rootStemNumericPrefix, documentSuffixes and rootStems), is a root document by a documentSuffixes entry other than the empty one: an extensionless name below the root (bin/changes, src/app/history) matches nothing

a path of two or more segments, some directory segment of which is one of docTreeRootsAnyDepth, whose final segment ends with .txt and is longer than it, is not one of the four-rule project-documentation rule's docTxtExcludedNames and does not begin with one of its docTxtExcludedPrefixes

rules.rule: the body of an admitted blob, after every screening step, whose final path segment ends with one of configurationExtensions or languageExtensions, equals one of sourceFileNames, or begins with one of sourceFileNamePrefixes, each compared case-sensitively as ASCII as sourceExtensions are. Configuration (YAML, TOML, JSON, HCL, protocol buffers, Dockerfiles, Makefiles and CMake files) is code-content, as configuration in a predecessor extension already is; it is source the project builds or runs from, never prose. No extractor runs: the class is by name and the body is admitted as whole-blob spans. The rule is read only in classDecision's second stage. It is not redacted (secretRedaction.appliesTo names no code-content body), so any detector match, configurationDetectors included, excludes it whole; activeContent.codeContentExemption names none of these extensions or names, so the body is scanned for active content as before

contentClassification.classDecision: a path's class is decided in two stages, after the denied-path rules and the detectors run over the path. Stage 1 is the predecessor's decision, unchanged: the five rules without an id (governance-text by governanceTextPaths, code-structure, code-content by sourceExtensions, project-documentation by exactly one of its four path rules, derived-composites) give a path at most one class, and a path they give two classes is indeterminate, exactly as before. A path Stage 1 places keeps that class and Stage 2 never reads it. Stage 2 reads only a path Stage 1 places in no class and does not find two classes for: if any directory segment of the path, after the fold, is one of vendoredDirectoryNames, the path is indeterminate; otherwise each of the three rules with an id (governance-text-by-name, project-documentation-extended, code-content-extended) is tried, and the path takes the class of the one that matches. A path two of them match is indeterminate (by construction governance-text-by-name and project-documentation-extended never both match: one requires a word of governanceTextTokens, the other forbids every word of docExcludedTokens). A path no rule places is indeterminate
contentClassification.indeterminate: every other admitted blob, including vendored documentation (a path with a directory in vendoredDirectoryNames that Stage 1 does not place), documents whose path carries a word of withheldTokens (decision, governance, policy, security, conduct, doctrine and principle records), documents and nested documentation the second stage refuses by withheldStems, evidenceWords or governanceStems, other than a root file the governance-text rule classifies, .txt files outside the docs-tree and docs-tree-text rules (and the excluded build and tooling names), notebooks (.ipynb), committed reports, symbolic-link entries the reader lists, and configuration or data in an extension or name none of sourceExtensions, configurationExtensions, languageExtensions, sourceFileNames or sourceFileNamePrefixes lists, is indeterminate and is treated as unclassifiable under unclassifiableExclusion: excluded from reading and from egress (fail closed), recorded hash-not-body, and never stored or rendered. Its path, object id and size remain code-structure, except that, for a repository whose visibility is private (sourceVisibility), its object id and size do not, under the code-structure rule

instructionTextRule.rule: the generator's instruction text is the text produced by exactly these two symbols at the prompt and schema versions a request names; it is not target content and is not read from a target. No other file or symbol of project:syzygy's repository is classified by this rule. Every detector in this policy applies to it before the first request of a run

publicSourceScope.classificationBasis: a class is decided at the runtime check from the origin of the content, tracked from where it entered the choke point (RFC5-14); a field name never assigns it. The field-level table in a public-target egress record is a gate on which fields may be carried and cannot confer a class, so content under a classed field name keeps the class of its origin (REQ-polaris-generation-025: composition preserves embedded classifications and origins)

targetMetadataRule.fieldsDerivedFrom: the sourcePopulation entry in packages/polaris-generation-core/src/pipeline.ts, read by this builder; the confirmed admission egress record's generated table classes the field sourcePopulation as target-metadata
targetMetadataRule.rule: the metadata the generator carries for each admitted-snapshot source, admitted or excluded alike, is exactly the fields listed and nothing else; reason is carried only for an excluded source and only as a member of the closed set that exclusionReasonSymbol names. No body, no content digest and no policy detail is carried under this rule. A path of an excluded source is not in the list and is not carried: the sourceId of an excluded source is an opaque identifier not derived from its path or body. [Inferred] this bytes-level rule is enforced only by the reader implementation, which the generator's lane is asked to write that way; nothing else in these bytes checks it
targetMetadataRule.reasonRule: the closed set of exclusion reasons is exactly the values of the exported constant named by exclusionReasonSymbol, read from code at the commit a run names; this policy lists no reason, so the set cannot differ from the values the constant declares. A reason outside that constant is not carried, and the generator's validator refuses it before a request. [Inferred] the constant and the validator are requested of the generator's lane and are not in code at this package's base; the package is not ready for an act until the constant exists (the builder fails closed while it is absent)

runProfileRule.rule: the run's reader questions and requested assets are classified only when they are the values of exactly these code-declared symbols, selected by a profile id a request carries (which id and which carrier is an open owner question: the base has no request field for one). A value from any other origin, including a run-directory file or an operator-supplied string, is unclassified under this scope and is not carried until a later policy version defines its origin and a validation. [Observed on the branch of PR #259] these symbols are readonly constants in dossier-profile.ts; [Observed on the base] the pipeline types readerQuestions as unknown, validates only requestedAssets and forwards readerQuestions unchanged, and no code reads a run-profile file. The typed reader-question validation the owner asked for is not yet in code and is not assumed here

publicSourceScope.detectors: every detector in this policy, and every detector in scopeDetectors, applies unchanged to every body under this scope, including inert code contexts; public visibility exempts nothing, and a match excludes the whole artifact with hash-not-body provenance (matchAction, RFC5-17), except where secretRedaction retains a body as redacted-span; every detector still runs over the complete body first. configurationDetectors run in addition, over the bodies, cited spans and agent text their rule names, and a match of one of them excludes the whole body

scopeDetectors.rule: these detectors are added to the policy's detectors for this scope only; the base scope and any sibling scope do not read them. Wherever this scope, its secretRedaction or its inheritedRules says every detector or a detector, these are included: they run over every path and every body under this scope, including inert code contexts, over a retained body's retained text and a cited span's text, and everywhere else this scope runs the policy's detectors. Each is read as the policy's detectors are (id, kind, pattern, flags), and a match is handled by matchAction and secretRedaction exactly as a match of the policy's detectors
scopeDetectors.consequence: [Inferred] a body whose only secret is a private key with a header the private-key-material literals do not list (EC, DSA, ENCRYPTED, PGP, RFC 4716, PuTTY, or a base64 PEM start), a password in a non-http connection string, or a listed vendor token, is no longer admitted: code-content and every class secretRedaction does not redact are excluded whole, and in project-documentation the URL form withholds its lines while the other two keep the body whole. The cost runs the other way: a body these match for a non-secret reason (a base64 certificate, a sample connection string with a password placeholder) is withheld where version 4 admitted it. config-secret-directive is paired with the redis.conf placement: [Inferred] a line opening, after blanks and any number of # comment marks, with requirepass, masterauth, tls-key-file-pass or tls-client-key-file-pass (quoted or not) and a value, or with an ACL rule user <name> (user quoted or not) carrying >password, <password, or # or ! with a 64-hex password hash, is withheld with its guard lines in project-documentation, as credential-bearing-url is, and withholds a body of any other class whole; a password written any other way in such a file (named mid-line, in a prose comment, as a rename-command target, as a module's own option, under a directive this pattern does not name, on a following line, or with a name or operator spelled through an escape or an inner quote) is not matched, and a prose or code line that opens with the word user and later has a blank and > or < is matched

configurationDetectors.rule: these detectors are added for this scope and run in addition to every detector in this policy and in scopeDetectors, which still run everywhere they ran. They run over the complete body of every blob classDecision's Stage 2 places (governance-text-by-name, project-documentation-extended and code-content-extended alike), including inert code contexts and comments, before any other step uses it; over every cited span of such a body; and over every text an agent session writes (a draft, an inventory, a verdict, a finding), wherever the policy's detectors screen it. They do not run over a body Stage 1 places, so no predecessor outcome for such a body changes. Each is read as the policy's detectors are (id, kind, pattern, flags, every match from every offset), and a match excludes the whole body or refuses the agent text (matchAction): a body these rules reach is never retained as redacted-span
configurationDetectors.consequence: [Inferred] a configuration body holding a password, secret, token or key under a quoted or unquoted key (JSON, YAML, TOML, HCL, Makefile and Dockerfile assignment forms; the keyword may sit anywhere in the key, so secret_key, SECRET_KEY_BASE, db_password_prod and a Docker auths entry's auth are matched; the predecessor's credential-assignment form reads neither a quoted JSON key nor such compound keys), a Kubernetes Secret manifest (whose base64 values no other detector reads), a Terraform variable whose name names a secret and which carries a default, a Dockerfile ENV or ARG naming a secret with a value, a netrc machine line, or an Authorization header value, is excluded whole. Residuals: a secret under a key that contains none of the keywords (for example a bare value in a list, or a key named only pass or pw), a value of fewer than eight characters or one containing whitespace or a quote, a value that opens with $, < or { (read as a reference or template), an encoded, encrypted (an Ansible Vault body) or split value, and a secret whose key and value sit on different lines are not matched. Keywords match inside longer words, so an author, tokenizer or passwordless key with a long value is matched and withholds its body (fail closed). Each pattern bounds its quantifiers before its value run, so matching from every offset stays linear in the body length

activeContent.rule: the base activeContentClassification, inertContextRule and the active-content condition of classificationSuccess apply unchanged to every admitted body, Markdown or not, except the steps codeContentExemption.rule and projectDocumentationExemption.rule lift for a body each exempts: a body neither exempts with an active-content form outside a valid inert code context is excluded whole as active content, and renderRule binds every body

codeContentExemption.appliesTo: a body this scope classifies code-content whose final path segment ends with one of exemptExtensions, compared case-sensitively as ASCII as sourceExtensions are
codeContentExemption.rule: such a body is admitted without the active-content scan: neither step 4 of classificationOrder, nor the active-content condition of classificationSuccess, nor the malformed-code-context exclusion applies to it, because the Markdown code-context profile does not describe source code (it reads a comparison such as a<b && c>d as an HTML tag, and an unpaired backtick in source as a code context that never closes). Every detector still runs over the whole body; the denied-path, strict-UTF-8, NUL and resource-limit rules are unchanged; a code-content body this exemption does not name, and a body of any other class that projectDocumentationExemption does not name, is scanned as before. The exemption reaches those three steps and nothing else: activeContentClassification.renderRule, and the encoding of selected text for its destination, still bind such a body at every place it reaches
codeContentExemption.renderCondition: a page is a document an HTML or SVG parser reads, and a page sink is a place where such a body's bytes, or a span of them, are written into a page. The exemption holds for a page sink only while it writes the body or span as text: every one of the characters & < > " ' is written as a character reference, the bytes are never parsed as Markdown or HTML and never mint a link, element, attribute, script or handler, and the page carries an enforced Content-Security-Policy, delivered before any of the body's bytes, whose directives are exactly default-src 'none', style-src 'unsafe-inline', base-uri 'none' and form-action 'none', each once with that one source, and at most one script-src, which comes with require-trusted-types-for 'script' and trusted-types 'none' and only then; no other directive is lawful, every token is written exactly as here in lower case, and a policy holding any non-ASCII byte, whitespace included, fails this condition. A script-src's source list is one or more 'sha256-<base64>' hash sources and nothing else. Each such hash is of one inline script with no src attribute that the renderer itself writes: its bytes are fixed in the renderer and derive from no body; it opens no connection and loads nothing (no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, sendBeacon, WebSocket, EventSource, WebTransport, RTCPeerConnection, Worker or window.open); it creates no element outside a list the renderer fixes, which never holds script, link, meta, base, form, iframe, object, embed, img, audio, video, source, track or style, and it sets no attribute that holds a URL; it never turns page text into code or markup (no eval, no Function, no string timer, no innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, setHTMLUnsafe, document.write, DOMParser or createContextualFragment, no handler attribute); it writes page text only as text; it navigates only by a fragment of the current page or an href the renderer wrote; and it stores no page text. Every page reads and navigates completely with scripts off. A consumer that cannot confirm this for a page sink scans the body as before for that sink, and excludes it whole there on a finding. Every other place such a body or a span of it reaches is not a page sink; egress governs it
codeContentExemption.egress: the exemption changes no egress or consent rule. At every place that is not a page sink (a review packet, a provider request, a discovery excerpt, a stored record), an exempt body or a span of it counts as screening-admitted code-content, reaches an agent session or a provider only under the rules that already govern code-content, and is encoded for that destination's format as renderRule requires

projectDocumentationExemption.appliesTo: a body this scope classifies project-documentation under one of the four path rules of the contentClassification rule whose class is project-documentation and which has no id (root-document, docs-tree, licenses-tree, owner-placement); a body the project-documentation-extended rule places is not exempted and is scanned as before
projectDocumentationExemption.rule: such a body is admitted without the active-content scan: neither step 4 of classificationOrder, nor the active-content condition of classificationSuccess, nor the malformed-code-context exclusion applies to it, because activeContentClassification.renderRule already says admitted Markdown is never rendered as HTML, so markup in it is inert bytes wherever this scope lets it reach a page. Every detector still runs over the whole body, and secretRedaction applies as before; the denied-path, strict-UTF-8, NUL and resource-limit rules are unchanged; a governance-text body is scanned as before. The exemption reaches those three steps and nothing else: activeContentClassification.renderRule, and the encoding of selected text for its destination, still bind such a body at every place it reaches
projectDocumentationExemption.renderCondition: codeContentExemption.renderCondition, read for a body this exemption names: the exemption holds for a page sink only while that condition holds for it, and a consumer that cannot confirm it for a page sink scans the body as before for that sink and excludes it whole there on a finding. Where that condition says egress governs every other place, it is this exemption's egress that governs, never codeContentExemption.egress
projectDocumentationExemption.egress: the exemption changes no egress or consent rule. At every place that is not a page sink (a review packet, a provider request, a discovery excerpt, a stored record), such a body or a span of it counts as screening-admitted project-documentation, reaches an agent session or a provider only under the rules that already govern that class (prerequisite.consentRule included), and is encoded for that destination's format as renderRule requires. Markup in it is data at every such place: an HTML comment, element or link destination is carried as text, never rendered or followed
projectDocumentationExemption.consequence: [Inferred] a README, release-notes or licence file whose only active-content finding is markup (an HTML badge, a centred heading, a placeholder written in angle brackets, an HTML comment) is admitted; the 2026-10-14 trial withheld two such root files for active content. The cost: markup that a reader of the upstream page does not see, such as an HTML comment, now reaches the review packet and agent sessions as text; and a documentation body version 4 withheld only for markup now carries the residuals of any admitted documentation body, a secret no detector matches and a secret beyond a guard line

activeContent.consequence: [Inferred] a source file whose only active-content finding was markup-like bytes outside a Markdown code context (a comparison, a generic type, a template literal, a string holding HTML) is admitted when its extension is exempt; the first public-target run (2026-10-08) withheld seven C files of its target for active content. A body a secret detector matches stays excluded whole

secretRedaction.appliesTo: a body of an admitted snapshot of a repository whose visibility is public (sourceVisibility), whose path this scope classifies in one of redactedClasses, after the denied-path, strict-UTF-8, NUL and resource-limit rules pass. A body of any other class, code-content included, is excluded whole on any detector match exactly as before, and so is a body of a private repository in every class: it is never retained as redacted-span. Text an agent session writes (a draft, an inventory, a verdict, a finding) is not such a body and is screened as before. A project-documentation body is in redactedClasses here only when classDecision's Stage 1 places it (one of the four path rules); a body any Stage 2 rule places is excluded whole on any detector match, in every class and under either visibility. Agent text is also screened by configurationDetectors, and a match refuses it
secretRedaction.rule: every detector runs over the complete transient body exactly as before, including inert code contexts. Here a detector's matches are every match it makes starting at any offset of the text, overlapping matches included, not only those a left-to-right non-overlapping scan reports. When at least one detector matches, none of the matches is from a detector in wholeArtifactDetectors, no line of the body matches wholeArtifactLinePattern (a regular expression applied to each line without its terminator: optional spaces or tabs, four or more '-', optional spaces or tabs, then BEGIN), and the body holds none of wholeArtifactFragments (compared exactly, case-sensitively), the body is retained as redacted-span (RFC5-17) instead of excluded whole. Lines are split at LF, CRLF or CR, as the generator counts lines; a match touches every line that holds any of its characters. A line a match touches, and guardLines lines before and after it, is a withheld line. Every detector then runs again over the retained text, which is the body with each withheld line replaced by an empty line of the same terminator; a match there excludes the whole artifact as excluded-artifact. A body with a match from a detector in wholeArtifactDetectors, a body with a line matching wholeArtifactLinePattern or holding one of wholeArtifactFragments, and a body with a match the consumer cannot place on lines, is excluded whole as before
secretRedaction.withheldLines: a withheld line is never stored, logged, rendered, sent, quoted, used to verify a quotation, or given to an agent session, and no digest of a withheld line, or of any part of one, is recorded. Wherever the retained body is shown or carried, each run of consecutive withheld lines is replaced by one marker that names the redaction and the total count of withheld lines in the body. The whole body's content digest and its Git object id remain recorded (RFC5-17 requires the digest), so a guess at short withheld lines can be checked against them; the target being public does not lift this residual
secretRedaction.citedSpanRule: a cited span (a start line and an end line of the body) that includes a withheld line is withheld whole, never shown in part, and every claim that depends on it renders Unknown with reason excluded-content (RFC5-17). A cited span that includes no withheld line is screening-admitted content of the body's class and is carried with the body's redaction count disclosed beside it; its own text is screened by every detector before it is carried, and a match withholds it
secretRedaction.provenance: the retained body's exclusion record is hash-not-body: the content digest of the complete body, its repository-relative path, policyId, policyVersion, the redaction class redacted-span, the id of each detector that matched, and the numbers of the withheld lines
secretRedaction.unchanged: the active-content scan, its malformed-code-context exclusion, activeContent.codeContentExemption and activeContent.projectDocumentationExemption run over the complete body exactly as their rules say, and an active-content finding in a body they do not exempt excludes the body whole; the content classes, the consent and egress rules and rawBodyHandling are unchanged; a withheld line changes no class
secretRedaction.consequence: [Inferred] a project-documentation body whose only detector matches are credential-assignment or credential-bearing-url forms (a token in a badge URL, a placeholder password in an example) keeps every line outside the matched lines and their guards; the trial of 2026-10-14 withheld all 41 cited spans of one README for one match on its first line. The cost: a body with a match is evidence that the file carries credentials, and whole-blob screening withheld everything in it; under this rule a secret in such a body that no detector matches (one beyond the guard line, or one continuing past it) is admitted

networkEgressRoutes: no network acquisition in the declared local-clone entry; private sources use no repository-host credential
classified and screened content only to the declared provider under SEC-2; no secrets
accessBoundary.routeRule: the networkEgress boolean stays false as the base reads it; the only permitted network use is these two routes, carried beside it, and a consumer that reads the boolean alone fails closed. The base accessBoundary is otherwise unchanged

rawBodyHandling.rule: storage is permitted only inside the local run directory outside git; no raw body logging or machine response; rendering is an editorial draft only. Content delivered to a provider must be classified and screened and the provider declared under SEC-2. Secrets never leave. Excluded or withheld private object identifiers and sizes are never rendered or sent and remain only in permitted local check records and review packets

publicSourceScope.inheritedRules: every other rule in this policy applies to this scope unchanged: detectors, matchAction and redactionClasses (except that secretRedaction retains a body of an admitted snapshot as redacted-span where its rule says so, and for such a body reads the detector condition of classificationSuccess as no detector matching its retained text), unclassifiableExclusion, activeContentClassification (except that, for a body activeContent.codeContentExemption or activeContent.projectDocumentationExemption exempts, its active-content forms are not scanned for and malformedContextAction does not apply; its renderRule binds every body) and the strict-UTF-8 and NUL rules. 'Every other rule' means the policy's rules outside any named scope object; the rules inside the base scope object, and inside any sibling scope object another act adds, do not govern this scope, and the other way round: the routes, boundaries, rawBodyHandling and rules written inside this object govern only the repositories in observedRepositories and never the base scope or a sibling scope. The base classificationOrder and classificationSuccess name the signed PWB grammar; under this scope they read: membership in the admitted snapshot replaces membership in a PWB phase, and the content-classification rules above replace the PWB closed extraction class, so a blob with no class under those rules has an unknown extraction class and is excluded whole (step 6), while a code-content body needs no extractor and is admitted as whole-blob spans. The dossier declared-source specification names this reading; adoption follows VIS-4 and changes no other inherited rule
publicSourceScope.selfReferenceRule: a target repository's policy, configuration or documentation text is never an input to this policy's evaluation (RFC3-30); authority for a pair is evaluated only for that pair and is never inherited from another pair, including through expectations keyed only by the observing project

prerequisite.requires: the RFC-0005 amendment that defines the class project-documentation in the closed vocabulary of RFC5-14
prerequisite.rule: the committed classification rule defines project-documentation; a malformed or unrecognized rule refuses rather than guessing its class
prerequisite.consentRule: A declared provider is required for agent-bound content. The committed policy classifies project-documentation without a separate class or consent act; an undefined or unreadable class remains excluded. No provider declaration overrides screening

phaseA.derivedSeedRule: after the root index is admitted, read only the README index named for each declared pillar root; use Git tree metadata, not bodies, to enumerate baseline openspec/specs/*/spec.md paths and top-level roster/*/butler.toml candidates
phaseA.output: revision-bound source manifest with extraction classes and sha256 digest

phaseB.manifestRule: manifest must validate against the signed PWB source grammar; it is derived data, not a separate owner-approved artifact

sourceAdmission.pathRuleScope: apply basename and prefix rules to the final segment, and suffix rules to the complete final segment, of each normalized repository-relative path; and apply directory-name rules to every segment of the path except the final one, so a path any of whose directories is named in deniedDirectoryNames is denied wherever that directory sits. Every rule compares case-insensitively, as the predecessor's rules are compared, and a denied path is never read

activeContentClassification.inertContextRule: markup-like bytes wholly inside a syntactically closed inline code span or fenced code block do not by themselves match an active-content form; they remain untrusted text, are scanned by every secret detector before parsing, and are context-encoded at every sink

markdownProfile.fencedOpener: zero to three spaces, then at least three identical backticks or tildes; a backtick opener info string contains no backtick
markdownProfile.fencedCloser: zero to three spaces, then the opener character repeated at least the opener length, then spaces only; the first qualifying closer ends the fence
markdownProfile.inlineOpener: outside a fence, a run of one or more backticks
markdownProfile.inlineCloser: the next backtick run of exactly the opener length; different-length runs are content and backslash does not escape a delimiter
markdownProfile.precedence: fenced context is recognized before inline context; the resulting mask applies only to active-content detection and never to secret detectors

activeContentClassification.renderRule: admitted Markdown is never rendered as HTML; selected text is encoded for its destination and code-context bytes never mint a link, element, attribute, script or handler

unclassifiableExclusion.appliesTo: every artifact excluded by classificationOrder step 6 for a reason other than a detector or active-content match: NUL byte, strict UTF-8 failure, malformed code context, unknown extraction class, parse failure or resource-limit failure

redactionClasses.vocabulary: closed by RFC5-17: excluded-artifact, redacted-span, unclassifiable-excluded
redactionClasses.unknownRendering: both emitted classes withhold the whole artifact, so every claim that depended on it renders Unknown with reason excluded-content and the exclusion count shown

classificationOrder: verify exact Git-object membership in the phase-A seed algorithm or the phase-B revision-bound manifest against the signed PWB grammar
reject denied path or unsupported encoding
run every detector over transient bytes before parsing
classify active content with Markdown code-context awareness; exclude a genuine active form and fail closed on malformed code context
parse only the closed extraction class assigned by the manifest
exclude the whole artifact on any match, NUL byte, strict UTF-8 failure, unknown extraction class, parse failure or resource-limit failure
classificationSuccess: a body is classifiable only when its normalized path is admitted by its current discovery phase, it decodes as strict UTF-8 without NUL, no detector matches anywhere in the complete body including inert code contexts, no active-content form occurs outside a valid inert code context, its extraction class is in the signed PWB closed set, and that extractor completes within declared deterministic limits
